newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly lower Thursday, with LME three month copper firmer in London but off its early highs, though the market remains bullish, traders said.
COMEX March copper was called to open unchanged to down 0.30cent a pound from Wednesday's close at 108.75 cents, after trading in a 108.00-108.55 range in overnight ACCESS trade.
COMEX copper stocks fell 478 short tons Wednesday to 17,491 short tons.
COMEX March copper ended at a new six month high Wednesday as the nearby spreads began to widen again.
The LME cash-to-three month spread was around $207 a tonne early Thursday, from $180 a tonne at Wednesday's close, and up from a low around $111.00 a tonne Tuesday.
Nearby spreads have been at or near the LME imposed limit of one percent of the previous day's cash settlement this week.

In the past three months copper prices have been recovering steadily from two year lows seen in mid-1996, when, after the Sumitomo scandal, prices fell to levels that restricted the supply of scrap onto the prompt market.
Seasonal demand and expected buying from the Far East are seen continuing to support copper prices, traders said.
